findings.topic: 1. Vault credential writers — who writes/updates vault profile copies
findings.detail: Grepped every writer touching vault profile dirs. Full inventory: (a) internal/authfile/authfile.go Backup()/BackupCurrent()(~L540)/ResnapshotOutgoing()(L576-601)/Restore()(~L711) — the vault<->live sync primitives; (b) cmd/caam/cmd/activate.go (the `caam activate`/switch command) is the ONLY caller that syncs a possibly-refreshed LIVE credential file back into a vault profile copy for Claude/Codex/Gemini, via `vault.ResnapshotOutgoing(fileSet, outgoing, profileName)` at activate.go:346, called from the switch flow at activate.go:339-353. Comment at activate.go:339-344 states explicitly this exists because 'Codex/ChatGPT rotate OAuth refresh tokens in place while a profile is active; without this, the vault copy of the outgoing profile goes stale.' (c) internal/refresh/refresh.go RefreshProfile() (L40-98) writes refreshed tokens into the vault path directly (not live) for codex/gemini, and additionally restores to the live location if the profile being refreshed was already active (L84-95) — this is invoked by `caam refresh`, `caam verify`, `caam activate` (activate.go:535, inside refreshIfNeeded L515-553), the TUI (internal/tui/model.go:1501), and the daemon (internal/daemon/daemon.go:666, internal/daemon/pool_refresher.go:31). (d) internal/refresh/refresh.go SyncVaultToIsolatedProfile()/syncCodexVaultToIsolated() (L321-368) copies vault->isolated-profile-dir for codex only (used by shallow-profile-style isolated homes, NOT the shared vault used by monitor). CRITICAL GAP: nothing in the repo periodically syncs the LIVE ~/.claude or ~/.codex directory into the vault while a profile merely sits active between switches — sync only fires (i) at the *next* `caam activate` call for the outgoing profile, or (ii) inside `RefreshProfile`'s explicit refresh call. There is no background/continuous live->vault sync daemon.
findings.evidence: activate.go:286-353,397,515-553; internal/authfile/authfile.go:576-601 (ResnapshotOutgoing calls v.Backup(fileSet, outgoing) at L600); internal/refresh/refresh.go:40-98,321-368; internal/daemon/daemon.go:666; internal/daemon/pool_refresher.go:17-44; internal/tui/model.go:1488-1501

findings.topic: 1b. authwatch package does NOT sync — detection only
findings.detail: internal/authwatch/authwatch.go (Tracker/Watcher, L1-650) hashes live auth files and compares them to vault profile hashes to detect 'unsaved auth' (e.g. a user ran `claude /login` directly, bypassing caam) — it only ever reports/suggests ('caam backup <tool> <profile>' at L379) and never writes to the vault itself. It is not wired into monitor.go at all (grep confirms internal/monitor never imports authwatch).
findings.evidence: internal/authwatch/authwatch.go:341-399 (GetStatus/SuggestedAction), no writes to vault anywhere in the file

findings.topic: 1c. ROOT-CAUSE CHAIN for stale vault tokens driving 401s
findings.detail: Because live->vault sync is switch-triggered-only (finding 1) and only ONE profile can be the live ~/.claude / ~/.codex at a time, every OTHER profile's vault copy is frozen at whatever token state existed the last time it was 'outgoing' at a switch. Claude access tokens are short-lived (health/expiry.go documents `claudeAiOauth.expiresAt` as Unix-ms, refreshed silently in-process by a running Claude Code binary — but Claude-side refresh is explicitly UNSUPPORTED/DISABLED inside caam itself, see finding 2). So: a profile not recently active has a vault copy whose access token has simply timed out with nothing in caam ever refreshing it — monitor.go reads that stale token verbatim (no expiry check, no refresh) and gets a genuine 401/403 from Anthropic, which alerts.go remaps to 'auth expired (re-login)'. This matches the user's report exactly: benson/cabot/saumil_2 (not recently active) => 401; arthur/saumil (apparently recently active, so vault holds a fresh, recently-resnapshotted token) => 429 (see finding 5 for why even a *valid* token gets rate-limited). It also explains why `caam shallow-spawn cc-cabot -- claude ...` 'comes up logged in with working /usage': shallow-spawn copies the same (possibly stale) vault token into an isolated HOME and launches a REAL Claude Code binary there, which — unlike caam's read-only probe — is able to silently refresh the token in-process on first 401 using its own refreshToken (Claude Code's internal refresh is not blocked by caam's `ClaudeRefreshDisabled` flag; that flag only blocks *caam* from calling the speculative endpoint itself). The interactive session thus 'heals' the token that caam's monitor cannot.
findings.evidence: internal/monitor/monitor.go:288-316 (readAccessToken — no expiry check, no refresh call anywhere in Refresh()); internal/refresh/claude.go:21-32 (ClaudeRefreshDisabled=true, comment: 'Claude Code handles token refresh internally; attempting external refresh may cause auth corruption'); docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md CLAUDE-006

findings.topic: 2. Existing OAuth-refresh infra (internal/refresh/) and why monitor doesn't use it
findings.detail: internal/refresh/ is a full, working refresh subsystem: refresh.go:RefreshProfile() (L40-98) dispatches per-provider; refreshCodex() (L116-134) does a REAL working refresh via RefreshCodexToken() (codex.go:24-78, POSTs to https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token) and persists via UpdateCodexAuth() (codex.go:81-123); refreshGemini() (refresh.go:136-194) similarly works and persists via health.Storage.UpdateProfile. refreshClaude() (refresh.go:100-114) is HARD-DISABLED: it unconditionally returns `&UnsupportedError{...}` without attempting anything. claude.go:21-32 documents why: the OAuth token endpoint (api.anthropic.com/oauth/token) is undocumented/speculative, and the team explicitly decided (docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md CLAUDE-006, dated 2026-01-21, bead caam-g8mv) that Claude Code handles its own refresh internally and external refresh risks 'auth corruption or undefined behavior.' Callers of RefreshProfile: cmd/refresh.go (`caam refresh`), cmd/verify.go (`caam verify`), cmd/activate.go (on switch, refreshIfNeeded), internal/tui/model.go (TUI keybinding), internal/daemon/daemon.go + pool_refresher.go (background daemon, requires the daemon process to be running). `internal/monitor/monitor.go` imports authpool and health but NOT internal/refresh, and never calls RefreshProfile anywhere — it is a pure read-only prober by design, decoupled from all the write-capable refresh machinery. It only runs if `caam daemon` is a running background process, which is not guaranteed / not mentioned as running in the user's repro.
findings.evidence: internal/refresh/refresh.go:40-134; internal/refresh/claude.go:14-32; internal/refresh/codex.go:24-123; docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md:127-150 (CLAUDE-006); internal/monitor/monitor.go:1-16 (imports) and full file (no refresh import/call); internal/daemon/pool_refresher.go:30-44; internal/daemon/daemon.go:451-491,644-686

findings.topic: 3. Full claude + codex credential schemas as understood by the repo
findings.detail: Claude (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, vault copy at `<vault>/claude/<profile>/.credentials.json`, legacy fallbacks `.claude.json` then `auth.json`): `{"claudeAiOauth": {"accessToken": string, "refreshToken": string, "expiresAt": number (Unix MILLISECONDS), "rateLimitTier": string, "subscriptionType": string, "scopes": [string]}}` per health/expiry.go:37-53,166-181 (claudeCredentialsJSON/claudeOAuthJSON) and per-CLAUDE-005 in docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md (verified correct: expiresAt present, in ms). BUT internal/usage/multi.go's ReadClaudeCredentials() (L228-279), which is what monitor.go actually calls via readAccessToken() (monitor.go:288-316), ONLY extracts `accessToken`/`accountId` — it never reads `expiresAt` or `refreshToken` at all, so the monitor has zero visibility into whether the token it's about to use is expired before making the HTTP call. Codex (`~/.codex/auth.json`, vault copy at `<vault>/codex/<profile>/auth.json`): supports both `{"tokens": {"access_token", "account_id"}}` (newer) and flat `{"access_token", "account_id", "refresh_token"}` (legacy), plus a non-OAuth `{"OPENAI_API_KEY": string}` mode that explicitly cannot use the usage endpoint (usage/multi.go:282-321, ReadCodexCredentials returns an error 'API key auth does not support usage fetch' in that case). Expiry schema per health/expiry.go:218-224: `expires_at` is Unix SECONDS (not ms, unlike Claude) at the top level or nested under `tokens`.

findings.topic: 4. Codex 'unknown' status — root cause confirmed as dead/unwired code in cmd/monitor.go, PLUS a second, more consequential source in health scoring
findings.detail: The trailing '| unknown' text after the Codex usage bar is `p.PoolStatus.String()` (render_table.go:71,76), which comes from `authpool.PoolStatus`. In cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:116, `var pool *authpool.AuthPool` is declared and NEVER assigned (no `authpool.NewAuthPool()`, no `.Load()`, no `.LoadFromVault()` call anywhere in the file) — it is passed straight into `monitor.WithAuthPool(pool)` at monitor.go:135 while still nil. In internal/monitor/monitor.go buildProfileState() (L318-344), `if m.pool != nil { state.PoolStatus = m.pool.GetStatus(...) }` is therefore always skipped, leaving the struct-literal default set two lines earlier: `PoolStatus: authpool.PoolStatusUnknown` (monitor.go:324). This is a 100%-reproducible, always-on bug: the CLI `caam monitor` command can NEVER show a real pool status for ANY profile of ANY provider — Claude rows don't show it only because usageUnavailable() (alerts.go:73-87) replaces the whole percent+status segment with the 'no usage: ...' text (render_table.go:61-66) whenever the fetch failed, masking the same 'unknown' that would otherwise appear. The '[WARN]' PREFIX (a completely separate signal — `healthEmoji(p.Health)`, render_table.go:56-58) is driven by `health.CalculateStatus()` (health/status.go:65-152) against whatever is in the *persisted* health.Storage (`m.health.GetProfile`, monitor.go:327-330) — NOT derived from the current usage-fetch result at all. Tracing where that persisted health data comes from: `cmd/root.go` primePlanTypes() (L403-413), called from `caam activate`(activate.go:560) and `caam next`(next.go:290), calls `healthStore.SetPlanType(tool, profileName, normalized)` which (health/storage.go:338-363) creates a brand-new `&ProfileHealth{}` (all zero fields — TokenExpiresAt IS ZERO, ErrorCount1h=0, Penalty=0) if none exists yet, sets ONLY PlanType, and persists it. Running CalculateHealth (health/status.go:74-152) on such a record: Factor1 expiry is IsZero => neutral (0 pts); Factor2 ErrorCount1h==0 => +0.3; Factor3 PlanType bonus: 'pro'/'team' => +0.2, 'enterprise' => +0.3, else +0; Factor4 Penalty subtract => 0. For any Claude Max/Pro/Plus account (normalizePlanType in root.go maps max/ultra/plus/premium -> 'pro'), the total score is EXACTLY 0.5, which the `else if score <= 0.5 { status = StatusWarning }` branch (status.go:124-126) classifies as Warning — a boundary bug (should be `< 0.5` or the whole 'no real data' case should map to StatusUnknown, not Warning). For plans with no bonus at all, score=0.3, also <=0.5 => Warning. Only 'enterprise' plans (score 0.6) clear the threshold to Healthy. NET EFFECT: any profile that has ever been switched to/activated via `caam activate`/`caam next` gets a permanently-seeded, TokenExpiresAt-less health record that `caam monitor`'s [WARN] badge will show as Warning FOREVER, completely independent of whether the just-completed usage probe succeeded (this explains the Codex rows showing '[WARN] ... 34% | unknown' despite a fully successful, healthy usage fetch).
findings.evidence: cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:116,135; internal/monitor/monitor.go:318-344; internal/monitor/render_table.go:55-77; internal/authpool/pool.go:136-145 (GetStatus returns PoolStatusUnknown if profile not tracked); internal/authpool/status.go:13-14; internal/health/status.go:74-152 (score math, esp. L121-126 the <=0.5 boundary); internal/health/storage.go:338-363 (SetPlanType); cmd/caam/cmd/root.go:376-413 (applyIdentityToHealth/primePlanTypes); cmd/caam/cmd/activate.go:560; cmd/caam/cmd/next.go:290

findings.topic: 5. 30s refresh loop + concurrent fetch interaction — no throttling/caching/backoff anywhere
findings.detail: internal/monitor/monitor.go Refresh() (L129-233) spawns one goroutine PER PROVIDER (L199-205: `go func(provider, tokens){ m.fetcher.FetchAllProfiles(...) }`), and internal/usage/multi.go FetchAllProfiles() (L55-201) spawns one FURTHER goroutine PER PROFILE inside that (L64-66: `for name, token := range profiles { go func(name, token string){...} }`), with a bare `sync.WaitGroup` and no semaphore, rate limiter, singleflight, or delay of any kind between requests. So for 5 Claude profiles, all 5 HTTP GETs to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` fire essentially simultaneously, every single tick of the monitor's ticker (default 30s, monitor.go:87/115/123; the CLI flag `--interval` defaults to 30s at cmd/monitor.go:52). Each `ClaudeFetcher` uses its own bare `&http.Client{Timeout: 30*time.Second}` (usage/claude.go:26-29) with no retry/backoff on 429/5xx — a 429 is simply surfaced as `API error: status 429` (usage/claude.go:86-89) and shown to the user with no cooldown/backoff logic engaged (the monitor DOES have a `loadCooldowns()`/`InCooldown` mechanism (monitor.go:149-152,272-286,337-340) but it is driven only by DB-recorded cooldown *events* from elsewhere in the app — nothing in the usage-fetch path itself ever calls into that system on a 429). The Claude usage endpoint is explicitly undocumented/'beta' (`anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` header, usage/claude.go:13-17,61; flagged as internal/experimental in docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md CLAUDE-007) — a burst of 5 concurrent requests from one machine, repeated every 30s indefinitely, is a materially different traffic pattern than the CLI's own occasional single-account `/usage` command, and is the most probable explanation for the 429s given the total absence of any client-side throttling in this code path (this is a code-evidence-based inference; live confirmation of the exact 429 trigger — per-token vs per-IP vs per-beta-flag rate limiting — would require an actual read-only probe, which was out of scope for this trace).
findings.evidence: internal/monitor/monitor.go:87,113-126,129-233 (esp. L162-205); internal/usage/multi.go:55-201 (esp. L60-66,182); internal/usage/claude.go:13-17,26-29,60-63,83-89; cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:52 (interval flag default); internal/monitor/monitor.go:149-152,272-286,337-340 (unrelated DB-cooldown system, not wired to live 429 responses)

findings.topic: 6. evaluateAlert/render path — which UsageInfo fields are rendered vs silently dropped
findings.detail: UsageInfo (usage/usage.go:27-76) has PrimaryWindow (Claude: 5-hour), SecondaryWindow (Claude: 7-day/weekly), TertiaryWindow (Claude: Opus-specific), and ModelWindows map (never populated by either fetcher — dead field for real traffic). ClaudeFetcher.Fetch (claude.go:99-138) DOES populate all three (five_hour->Primary, seven_day->Secondary, opus->Tertiary) from the real API response. CodexFetcher.Fetch (codex.go:163-196) populates PrimaryWindow/SecondaryWindow from `rate_limit.primary_window`/`secondary_window` plus Credits; it has no TertiaryWindow/model-specific concept at all in the current schema. evaluateAlert() (monitor/alerts.go:34-66) and usagePercent()/MostConstrainedWindow() (alerts.go:110-123; usage/usage.go:238-269) COLLAPSE all of Primary/Secondary/Tertiary/ModelWindows down to a single 'most constrained' percentage — whichever window has the highest utilization becomes THE number shown. The TABLE renderer (render_table.go:60-77) then shows exactly ONE progress bar + ONE percent for that single most-constrained window; it NEVER separately displays PrimaryWindow (5h) vs SecondaryWindow (weekly) vs TertiaryWindow (opus/Fable) — a user cannot tell from `caam monitor`'s table/brief/alerts output whether they're close to the 5-hour cap or the weekly cap, only that 'something' is at X%. The JSON renderer IS the one path that already exposes everything: encodeJSONState() (render.go:111-152) embeds the full `*usage.UsageInfo` verbatim (`Usage: p.Usage`, jsonProfile struct field `Usage interface{}` L61), so `caam monitor --format json` already contains `primary_window`/`secondary_window`/`tertiary_window` with their own utilization/resets_at per-window — this data is fetched and present in memory (ProfileState.Usage, monitor/state.go:22) but simply never surfaced by the three human-facing renderers (table/brief/alerts). Concretely: five_hour (Primary) IS already fetched but not displayed distinctly in the table; opus/Tertiary IS already fetched (for Claude) but not displayed distinctly either — both are only reachable indirectly via whichever happens to be 'most constrained', or via raw JSON.
findings.evidence: internal/usage/usage.go:27-76,238-269; internal/usage/claude.go:99-138; internal/usage/codex.go:163-196; internal/monitor/alerts.go:34-66,110-123; internal/monitor/render_table.go:60-77; internal/monitor/render.go:57-73,111-152; internal/monitor/state.go:19-28

findings.topic: D4 (per-model usage: Fable/GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark) — not present in either schema today
findings.detail: Grepped the entire repo (case-insensitive) for 'fable' — zero hits outside this task's framing; it is not an existing caam concept. The live Claude usage endpoint schema the repo already parses (claude.go:33-42) only ever returns `five_hour`/`seven_day`/`opus` — there is no per-arbitrary-model breakdown; 'opus' (TertiaryWindow) is the closest existing 'premium model' bucket, and it is unknown/unverified whether a hypothetical 'Fable' model would appear under a similarly-named field or not appear at all (would require a live read-only probe against an account actually using that model to observe the real JSON — out of scope for this code trace). Codex's schema (codex.go:36-58) has `plan_type`, `rate_limit.{primary,secondary}_window`, and `credits` — no model-name-keyed breakdown whatsoever, so a 'GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark' figure is not obtainable from the currently-called endpoint at all, only (maybe) from a different, not-yet-integrated endpoint. `UsageInfo.ModelWindows` exists as a field (usage/usage.go:52-55) precisely for this kind of future use but is populated nowhere in the codebase today.
findings.evidence: internal/usage/claude.go:32-42; internal/usage/codex.go:36-58; internal/usage/usage.go:52-55 (ModelWindows, unpopulated); repo-wide grep for 'fable' = no matches

hypotheses.hypothesis: The 401/403 'auth expired (re-login)' rows are caused by genuinely stale (past-expiry) access tokens sitting in NON-currently-active vault profile copies, because live->vault sync only happens at the next `caam activate` switch (via ResnapshotOutgoing) and caam never performs Claude-side token refresh itself (explicitly disabled, docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md CLAUDE-006) — the accounts are not actually broken/logged-out, just holding a token caam's own probe cannot refresh, unlike a real running Claude Code process (as shallow-spawn demonstrates).
hypotheses.evidence: internal/monitor/monitor.go:288-316 (no expiry check/refresh anywhere in the probe path); cmd/caam/cmd/activate.go:339-353 (only sync point, switch-triggered); internal/refresh/claude.go:14-32 (Claude refresh hard-disabled by design, not a bug to 'fix' by re-enabling); user's own repro (shallow-spawn works) is consistent with this — it does NOT rule out a competing/complementary hypothesis (a genuinely revoked/logged-out account would also fail in shallow-spawn, so the passing repro is decent evidence against 'account revoked' and in favor of 'stale-but-recoverable token').

hypotheses.hypothesis: The 429 responses are caused by caam's own request pattern (5 concurrent GETs per tick, no throttling/backoff, every 30s, against an undocumented/beta-flagged endpoint not designed for this call volume) rather than any real per-account quota exhaustion.
hypotheses.evidence: internal/usage/multi.go:55-201 and internal/monitor/monitor.go:162-205 show zero rate limiting of any kind; internal/usage/claude.go:13-17 anthropic-beta header marks the endpoint as internal/experimental (docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md CLAUDE-007). This is inferred from code absence-of-throttling, not from an observed live 429 response body/headers (e.g. Retry-After) — a single bounded read-only GET per affected account, spaced out per the security rules, would let a future diagnosis agent confirm whether 429 is per-token, per-IP, or tied to concurrency, which this code-only trace could not settle.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The '[WARN]' badge shown in `caam monitor`'s table is effectively meaningless/always-on for any profile that has ever been switched to via `caam activate`/`caam next` on a non-enterprise plan, due to a boundary bug in health.CalculateHealth's score<=0.5 threshold combined with SetPlanType() seeding TokenExpiresAt-less health records — independent of the real-time usage-fetch outcome shown in the same row.
hypotheses.evidence: internal/health/status.go:74-152 arithmetic traced by hand for a 'pro' plan record with zero expiry/errors/penalty yields score=0.5 exactly, landing in the `<= 0.5` Warning branch (status.go:124-126); internal/health/storage.go:338-363 SetPlanType() confirmed to create exactly such a record; cmd/root.go:403-413 + cmd/activate.go:560 + cmd/next.go:290 confirmed as the only callers that seed it.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The trailing '| unknown' pool-status text on every profile row (visible on Codex rows, masked on failed Claude rows by the 'no usage:' branch) is unconditional dead-code behavior in the CLI, not data-dependent at all.
hypotheses.evidence: cmd/caam/cmd/monitor.go:116,135 — `var pool *authpool.AuthPool` is declared and never assigned before being passed to `monitor.WithAuthPool(pool)`; internal/authpool/pool.go:136-145 GetStatus on a nil-guarded path is never even reached since internal/monitor/monitor.go:333 checks `if m.pool != nil` first, so the struct-literal default `authpool.PoolStatusUnknown` (monitor.go:324) is what always renders.

open_questions: Live confirmation needed (within the workflow's read-only GET budget) of the exact 429 trigger for Claude's oauth/usage endpoint: is it per-access-token, per-source-IP, or purely a function of concurrent request count/frequency? Code shows zero throttling either way, but only a live probe (e.g. one single sequential GET per affected profile, spaced >=2s, vs the current 5-concurrent pattern) can distinguish 'this endpoint just has a low global rate limit' from 'caam's own burst pattern is the trigger.'

Does the real Claude usage API ever expose a distinct 'Fable' model window (vs generic 'opus'), and does the Codex usage API expose any model-specific breakdown (e.g. via a different endpoint than /wham/usage)? Not answerable from static code — the only two fetchers in this repo do not request or parse any such field today, so beads for D4 should default to 'graceful omit' pending a live read-only response inspection.

Is a `caam daemon` process typically running for these accounts? If yes, internal/daemon proactively refreshes Codex/Gemini tokens (not Claude) on a schedule via authpool.Monitor/PoolRefresher, which would explain why Codex usage came back healthy while several Claude profiles show real 401s — but nothing in the monitor CLI code path checks or depends on daemon liveness, so this should be verified against the user's actual running-process state before beads assume the daemon is/isn't active.

Should health.CalculateHealth's scoring formula/threshold be fixed at the source (internal/health/status.go), or should internal/monitor specifically stop consuming health.Storage's persisted (mostly plan-type-only) records altogether and instead derive its status badge from something monitor-local (e.g. the current probe's own success/failure + Alert, or a direct vault-credentials expiry parse like daemon.go's getProfileHealth()/root.go's buildProfileHealth() already do) — fixing the shared health.CalculateHealth formula risks changing behavior for other consumers (cmd/root.go status display, daemon proactive-refresh decisions, rotation/selector scoring) that also depend on it, so bead authors should decide the blast radius explicitly.

For the deliverable-1 fix shape (D2): given Claude-side token refresh is deliberately hard-disabled repo-wide for safety reasons already documented in docs/CLAUDE_AUTH_INVENTORY.md (CLAUDE-006), does the user want the beads to (a) leave that safety decision untouched and instead have `caam monitor` opportunistically resnapshot the LIVE credentials of whichever profile is CURRENTLY active into its own vault copy each tick (a pure file-copy, not an OAuth call, extending the existing ResnapshotOutgoing pattern) so at least the live profile never shows stale-401, while accepting that non-active profiles remain only as fresh as their last switch-away; or (b) reconsider enabling a real Claude refresh call after all (reopening the exact risk the team previously closed off)? This is a product decision, not something resolvable by code tracing alone.
